strings: Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
Blocks of stone arranged in a tile-like pattern, odd, really, how it looks like real stone too, because it is!
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
A canister for the storage of gas.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
The HT-451, a torque rotation-based, waste disposal unit for small matter. This one seems remarkably clean.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A simple fishing hook. Don't expect to hook onto anything without one.
It has some unsavory stains on it...
You shouldn't see this. Report it please.
A console intended to send requests to different departments on the station.
Perfectly designed to be comfortable to sit on, and hellish to sleep on.
A basin used to grow plants in.
A luxurious double bed, for those too important for small dreams.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A seedy table for seedy dealings in seedy places.
This station is just crawling with bugs.
What did I say about leaning on the glass tables? Now you need surgery.
A low-end laptop often used for personal recreation.
A dispenser of low-potency virus mutagenic.
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
Now you see me, now you don't...
Sturdy exterior hull plating that separates you from the uncaring vacuum of space.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
\"In case of emergency, please use the stairs.\" Thus, always use the stairs.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
A lightweight lift platform. It moves.
Thick, tough flooring created with multiple layers of metal.
A fake, cheap looking, plastic tree. Perfect for people who kill every plant they touch.
Produces a single chemical at a given volume. Must be plumbed. Most effective when working in unison with other chemical synthesizers, heaters and filters.
It's coarse and rough and gets everywhere.
All engineering related spawners go here
Flooring that shows its contents underneath. Engineers love it!
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
A window made out of a plasma-silicate alloy and a rod matrix. It looks hopelessly tough to break and is most likely nigh fireproof.
A tank full of industrial welding fuel. Do not consume.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
Often used to flavor food or make people sneeze.
A shutter with a thick see-through polycarbonate window.
A wall-mounted first aid station, designed to treat minor injuries - just stick your hand in and try to relax.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
The HS-452. Installed in the 2550s by the Nanotrasen Hygiene Division, now with 2560 lead compliance! Passively replenishes itself with water when not in use.
This is used to lie in, sleep in or strap on.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
A standard metal table frame covered with an amazingly fancy, patterned cloth.
For the bulkier art pieces, hand-picked by the curator.
Used to monitor the station's atmospherics sensors.
A box full of lethal shotgun shells, designed for shotguns.
Used to access the various cameras on the outpost.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
A charging dock for energy based weaponry, PDAs, and other devices.
A modified version of the Type 5 laser gun. Fires entirely harmless bolts of directed energy. Safe AND entertaining to fire with abandon.
The herpes of arts and crafts.
Keeps idiots like you from walking into an open elevator shaft.
A transit tube for moving things around.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
Excellent for securing things away from grubby hands.
In Greek myth, Prometheus stole fire from the Gods and gave it to 		humankind. The jewelry he kept for himself.
A thin layer of dust coating the floor.
All the finest of miscellaneous electronics one could ever need! Not responsible for any injuries caused by reckless misuse of parts.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with identification modification programs.
A button used for the explicit purpose of opening an airlock.
They look like the remains of something... alien. They have a strange aura about them.
A bar sign which has not been initialized, somehow. Complain at a coder!
A photo frame to commemorate crewmembers that distinguished themselves in the line of duty. WARNING: unauthorized tampering will be severely punished.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
A frame for constructing your own computer. Or console. Whichever name you prefer.
A nasty looking shard of glass.
A console used for high-priority announcements and emergencies.
This device is used to trigger station functions which require more than one ID card to authenticate, or to give the Janitor access to a department.
A cheap Nanotrasen medical laptop, it functions as a medical records computer. It's bolted to the table.
It's a storage unit for emergency breath masks and O2 tanks.
A set of Nanotrasen regulations for keeping law, order, and procedure followed within their space stations.
Contains all the paper you'll never need.
It's a normal black ink pen.
Used for scanning and alerting when someone enters a certain proximity.
A board for linking evidence to crimes.
Seems like this one won't hatch.
It's a storage unit for fire-fighting supplies.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Engineering department is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Security department is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the Medbay is.
A direction sign, pointing out which way the arrivals shuttle dock is.
I have a mouth and I must eat.
Don't jump on it, or do, I'm not your mom.
A high-capacity superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit.
A large pile of pillows. Jump on it!
This Reaction Chamber comes with a bit of buffer to help get you started.
An adorable stuffed toy that resembles a space carp.
A basic handheld radio that communicates with local telecommunication networks.
Contains condensed capsaicin for use in law \"enforcement.\"
A door remote control switch for the engineering security airlocks.
This device recharges energy-dependent lifeforms, like cyborgs, ethereals, and MODsuit users.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
A heavy-duty industrial laser, often used in containment fields and power generation.
Used to request supplies from cargo.
A sign labelling an area where laws are uploaded to the station's AI and cyborgs.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
WARNING: These devices are extremely dangerous and can cause blindness and skin irritation.
A terrible, terrible thing. It's really awful!
It's a storage unit for rad-protective suits.
A more portable sort of aquarium to store various fishes in, unless they're too big or there're too many of them.

A sign labelling an area where research and science is performed.
This relatively unknown vending machine delivers clothing for Atmospherics Technicians, an equally unknown job.
A wooden shelf, used to hold seeds preventing them from germinating early.
Checked out books MUST be returned on time.
Contains blood used for transfusion. Must be attached to an IV drip.
Over 87% of humans are right handed. That figure is much lower 		among humans missing their right arm.
Oh, so this is a dress-up game now.
A nondescript pair of tough jeans.
A poster encouraging you to help fellow crewmembers.
Used to create a convincing illusion of a different background.
A blood sausage, battered and deep fried. Commonly served with fries as a quick and simple snack on the streets of Zagoskeld.
A remote control switch for the brig exterior doors.
A remote control switch for the brig interior doors.
A rectangular steel crate. It seems to be painted to look like gold.
A tank of plasma gas designed specifically for use as internals, particularly for plasma-based lifeforms. If you're not a Plasmaman, you probably shouldn't use this.
Used to remotely locate or lockdown exosuits.
The label's written in Cyrillic. All you can make out is the name and a word that looks vaguely like 'Vodka'.
A shot glass - the universal symbol for bad decisions.
A vending machine for when you really wish you weren't at work right now.
A standard-measure shipping container for bulk transport of goods. This one prominently features Cybersun's logo, and so presumably could be carrying almost anything.
Deploy to designate the landing zone of the auxiliary base.
A piece of hot spicy meat.
Fresh footlong ready to go down on.
Uses shearing action and growth inducers to reshape your coworkers external features!
A bright blue cat plush with neon pink hair, here to hand out kisses wherever kisses need be. Usually found near its home habitat, the tram.
A piece of headgear used in dangerous working conditions to protect the head. Comes with a built-in flashlight AND welding shield! The bulb seems a little smaller though.
A display case for prized possessions.
Keeps an area from being fried by Edison's Bane.

The \"Dynamic Rapid-Apprehension of the Guilty Network\" translocation shotgun (or DRAGnet for short) is a revolution in law enforcement technology. 		By syncing the weapon to a DRAGnet beacon, the bluespace transportation fields produced by the weapon's 'snare' function can rapidly exfiltrate an entire 		security squad, with criminal in tow. Otherwise, the weapon is an entirely nonlethal apprehension tool. Exceptionally useful for nonlethal close-quarters battle.
Known for their soft wool and use in sacrificial rituals. Big fan of grass.
This carp has been created as a decoration in the biodome. You feel you should come and see him.
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with research programs.
A metallic-plastic composite breaching hammer, looks like a whack with this would severly harm or tire someone.
A box full of standard firing pins, to allow newly-developed firearms to operate.
An industrial grinder used to process meat and other foods. Keep hands clear of intake area while operating.
A spring loaded gun designed to fit syringes, used to incapacitate unruly patients from a distance.

There is a small label that reads \"For Emergency use only\" along with details for safe use of the jaws of recovery. 		The lock seems to require...a surgical drill bit to unlock? You have no idea who thought this was a good idea.
This humble little stick usually carries a frozen treat, at the moment it seems freed from this Atlassian burden.
This vending machine might not dispense meat, but it certainly dispenses chef related clothing.
A pickaxe that's been left to rust.
A headset for the trained staff of the medbay.
Glass which seems to have rods or something stuck in them.
Used for emergency sealing of hull breaches, while keeping areas accessible.

One of the more successful achievements of the Nanotrasen Corporate Warfare Division, their nuclear fission explosives are renowned for being cheap to produce and devastatingly effective. Signs explain that though this particular device has been decommissioned, every Nanotrasen station is equipped with an equivalent one, just in case. All Captains carefully guard the disk needed to detonate them - at least, the sign says they do. There seems to be a tap on the back.
A rectangular steel crate. It seems to be painted to look like silver.
The largest canvas available on the space market. You'll need a larger frame to put it on a wall.
A heavy, metal trashcart with wheels.
Dispenses pipes that will ultimately be used to move trash around.
Useful for killing pests of all sizes.
There is a small label that reads \"For Emergency use only\" along with details for safe use of the tool. As if.
A sign that warns of high-power testing equipment in the area.
A metal tray to lay food on.
A general purpose Chef's Knife made by SpaceCook Incorporated. Guaranteed to stay sharp for years to come.
Used to knock out the Bartender.
A bouquet of roses. A bundle of love.
A metal shaker to mix drinks in.
A bluespace anchor for chemicals. Does not require power. Use a multitool linked to a Chemical Recipient on this machine to start teleporting reagents.
Contains a large reservoir of the good stuff.
It's milk. White and nutritious goodness!

An advanced machine equipped with state of the art bomb prediction software that's capable of implosion-compressing raw anomaly cores into finished artifacts. 	Comes with a built-in stabilization and sound-supressant field that consumes a lot of power to prevent obnoxious shaking and sounds heard station-wide, as not to wake up any dorms users.
It's pie cream from a cream pie.
A cheap replica of The Stinger. It isn't nearly as powerful, no wonder it's wielder died.
A tank full of a high quantity of welding fuel. Keep away from open flames.
Used to create condiments and other cooking supplies.
A freestanding medical kiosk, which can provide a wide range of medical analysis for diagnosis.
An annoying clock that keeps you sane through tireless nights.
The power control station for a bluespace teleporter. Used for toggling power, and can activate a test-fire to prevent malfunctions.
It would seem it vends dyes, and other stuff to make you pretty.
A refrigerated storage unit for petri dishes.
Spooky! It's got delicious coffee flavouring!
Spooky! It's got delicious calcium flavouring!
A compact micro-machine capable of amplifying weak subspace transmissions.
A sophisticated analyzer capable of analyzing cryptic subspace wavelengths.
An adorable stuffed toy of a medihound.
A specially-reinforced camera with a long lasting battery, used to monitor the bomb testing site. An external light is attached to the top.
A pneumatic waste disposal unit. This one leads to the frozen exterior of the moon.
A warning sign which reads 'DISPOSAL: LEADS TO SPACE'.
A skateboard. It can be placed on its wheels and ridden, or used as a radical weapon.
A sign labelling an area where engineers work.
Besides being almost too large for a standard frame, the AI can accept these as a display from their internal database after you've hung it up.
A stuffed toy that resembles your purple coworkers. Mmm, yeah, in true plasmaman fashion, it's not cute at all despite the designer's best efforts.
Used to retrieve cell lines from organisms. Don't worry, it won't sting.
A small set of steps you can use to reach high shelves or climb onto platforms, just watch your ankles.
A sign that warns of potentially reactive chemicals nearby, be they explosive, flammable, or acidic.
It's a useless heap of junk... or is it?
Ian is love, Ian is life.
The world of janitalia wouldn't be complete without a mop.
This is the alpha and omega of sanitation.
Used by engineering staff to see underfloor objects such as cables and pipes.
A vending machine for specialised clothing for members of Command.
Something wrapped in silky spider web.
A handheld device used for detecting and measuring radiation pulses.
A telescreen with access to the research division's camera network.
It has a Nanotrasen symbol on it, and was woven with a revolutionary new kind of thread guaranteed to have 0.01% permeability for most non-chemical substances, popular among most modern captains.
It's a storage unit for gloves for use in the boxing ring.
It is said that the ancient Appalachians used these stoneware jugs to capture lightning in a bottle.
A pair of winter boots with special grips on the bottom, designed to prevent slipping on frozen surfaces.
Controls a stacking machine... in theory.
A telescreen that connects to the auxiliary base's camera.
Used for repairing or building APCs.
A frame for a defibrillator mount. Once placed, it can be removed with a wrench.
A shell assembly that can be completed by screwdrivering it.

\"This is a plaque in honour of our comrades on the G4407 Stations. Hopefully TG4407 model can live up to your fame and fortune.\" Scratched in beneath that is a crude image of a meteor and a spaceman. The spaceman is laughing. The meteor is exploding.
A dish full of food slop for your bowl.
A relic of a failed rebellion.
A self cleaning vending machine capable of dispensing clothing for janitors.
A telescreen that connects to the interrogation room's camera.
A machine designed to send civilian bounty targets to centcom.
A standard-measure shipping container for bulk transport of goods. This one is from Donk Co. and so could be carrying just about anything- although it's probably just Donk Pockets.
A mug to display your corporate pride.
These clunky gauntlets allow you to drag things with more confidence on them not getting nabbed from you.
It's a wriggling worm from a can of fishing bait. You're not going to eat it, are you?
Central Command standard issue inspection device. 		Used for precision scans to determine if an item contains, or is itself, contraband.
A white knight chess piece. It can hop over other pieces, moving in L shapes. A white kni- oh. Hah!
A machine for all your detective needs, as long as you need clothes.
You can drill using this item. You dig?
Used to view crew member accounts and purchases.
Hello, you've reached Arnold's pizza shop. I'm not here now, I'm out killing pepperoni.
A vending machine for dispensing chemistry related clothing.
A double sided angled mirror for reflecting laser beams.
A pipe, for smoking. Probably made of meerschaum or something.
All you need to destroy those pesky weeds and pests.
A set of 8 Nanotrasen-approved floppy disks in individual packaging.
Renault's bed! Looks comfy. A foxy person needs a foxy pet.
This space is blocked off by a crude assortment of planks.
A freezer containing packs of blood.
An interface for ordering fresh produce and other. A far more expensive option than the botanists, but oh well.
The cap of a large mushroom.
An ordinary cardboard box with holes cut in the sides.
A hefty machine that, when supplied with iron and glass, will periodically create a drone shell. Does not need to be manually operated.
A sign labelling an area where the Psychologist works, they can probably help you get your head straight.
A pack of Nanotrasen brand rolling papers.
A simple vending machine suitable to dispense well tailored science clothing. Endorsed by Space Cubans.
It has a picture of drinking glasses on it.
A box full of oxygen goodies.
Dr. Miles Manners is just your average wasp-themed super hero by day, but by night he becomes DR. BEES!
Drainage inlet embedded in the floor to prevent flooding.
Autonomous Power Loader Unit Subtype Paddy. A Modified MK-I Ripley design intended for light security use.
A heavy wooden box, which can be filled with a lot of ores or boulders
A pile of scrap metal. It seems damaged beyond repair.
Don't shine it in your eyes!
A stationary computer. This one comes preloaded with art programs.
A mysterious gateway built by unknown hands, it allows for faster than light travel to far-flung locations.
A specialized medical kit for when the ordnance lab -spontaneously- burns down.
A banner with the logo of the red deity.
Used to treat toxic blood content and radiation poisoning.
A box of crayons for all your rune drawing needs.
A machine with some drapes and a camera, used to update security record photos. Requires Law Office access to use.
The supply department's overfed yet still beloved dog.
An industrial computer integrated with a camera-assisted rapid construction drone.
A headset with a commanding channel.
Used to send criminals to the Labor Camp.
It's an airtight container for storing medication.
A packet of extremely pungent seeds.
Boil 'em! Mash 'em! Stick 'em in a stew!
These seeds grow into tomato plants.
These seeds grow into grass. Yummy!
These seeds grow into common ambrosia, a plant grown by and from medicine.
These may, or may not, grow into wheat.
These seeds grow into pumpkin vines.
This mycelium grows into tower-cap mushrooms.
A display case with an ID-card swiper. Use your ID to purchase the contents. Meant for the bartender and chef.
For the enterprising botanist on the go. Less efficient than the stationary model, it creates one seed per plant.
A sterile satchel with chemist colours.
Turn your Good Assistant Points punchcards in here for a payout based on the amount of punches you have, and get a new card!
Use this if your friends left you behind.
An old decommissioned scanner, permanently scuttled.
An unsterilized machine for dispensing virology related clothing.
Not known for their pleasant disposition. This one seems a bit more hardy to the cold.
Keeps cold things cold and hot things cold.
A defunct genetics machine for merging foreign DNA with a subject's own.
An entire book on how to not turn yourself into a fly mutant.
A comfy-looking cat bed. You can even strap your pet in, in case the gravity turns off.
A pole with powerful mounted lights on it. Due to its high power draw, it must be powered by a direct connection to a wire node.
A telescreen that connects to the bomb test site's camera.
The POWER that gamers CRAVE! In partnership with Vlad's Salad.
Essentially a big block of metal that you can hammer other metals on top of, crucial for anyone working metal by hand.
A cheap statue of sandstone for a greyshirt.
This carp has been created as a decoration in the biodome. You feel you should love him and believe him.
An adorable stuffed toy of a Medidrake.
Because using pans is for pansies.
A basic energy-based laser carbine that fires concentrated beams of light which pass through glass and thin metal.
An basic energy-based laser auto-carbine that rapidly fires weakened, concentrated beams of light which pass through glass and thin metal.
Used to grind things up into raw materials and liquids.
An adorable stuffed toy that resembles a very determined spacefaring green lizardperson. To infinity and beyond, little guy. This one fills you with nostalgia and soul.
The gaping maw of a dead, titanic monster.
An automated announcement system that handles minor announcements over the radio.
A crafting bench fitted with tools, securing mechanisms, and a steady surface for blacksmithing.
An outdated hotdog vending machine, its prices stuck to those of 20 or so years ago.
This is my BROOMSTICK! It can be used manually or braced with two hands to sweep items as you move. It has a telescopic handle for compact storage.
Strangely ancient technology used to help provide rudimentary eye cover. Larger than average enhanced shielding blocks flashes.
An old NT branded sleeper, decommissioned after the lead acetate incident. None of the functional machinery remains inside.
It's a sick-looking goose, probably ate too much maintenance trash. Best not to move it around too much.
A teleportation matrix used to retrieve boulders excavated by mining NODEs from ore vents.
A small rack for storing coffeemaker cartridges.
A scaffold for bees to build honeycomb on.
She's the queen of bees, BZZ BZZ!
A solid wall of web, dense enough to block air flow.
A Wiz-Off deck. Fight an arcane battle for the fate of the universe: Draw 5! Play 5! Best of 5! A rules card is attached.
Remains of some unfortunate mecha. Completely irreparable, but perhaps something can be salvaged.
A pump bottle containing caramelized sugar, also known as caramel. Do not lick.
A pump bottle containing korta syrup. A sweet, sugary substance made from crushed sweet korta nuts.
A remote control switch for a mounted igniter.
It's got ELECTROLYTES! Only to be consumed in the freedom of a dispenser zone. The punch zone is practiced without conflicting with institutional policies, public safety, or daily operations.
A heretical poster depicting the titular star of an equally heretical book.
Get a load, or give, of these all natural Xenos!
A much larger version of the hand-held scanner. A charred label warns about its destructive capabilities.
An engine that releases a large bluespace burst to propel it.
A comfortable, secure seat. It has a more sturdy looking buckling system, for smoother flights.
A wall mounted safe containing space suits. Will only open in emergencies.
